sources.entry: Runtime - AI taskmate and take control of the web & your office tools

summary.one_liner: Runtime is a desktop AI agent (built with Tauri) that drives Chromium-based browsers using predefined "skills" to work with the web and office tools such as Gmail, Notion, and Amazon.
summary.what_it_does: Runtime runs AI-driven tasks inside Chromium-based browsers such as Chrome and Edge, with Firefox, Brave, Dia, and Comet listed as coming later. Instead of having an LLM reason over the live DOM at runtime, it uses hand-crafted "skills": ordered step recipes (navigate, wait for selector, click, type, scroll, extract list) that target elements by tag attributes present after Blink renders the page. The README gives an amazon.com search_products skill as an example. Actions run in the user's own logged-in browser session. The README also describes a research mode that gathers, ranks, and cites sources in a "tabs" tab, multi-step email triage and replies, and sending results to Apple Notes. Setup uses a Gemini API key in a .env file.
use_cases: automate email triage and replies in Gmail
amazon product search and price extraction
run multi-step browser tasks with an AI agent
send browser results to Apple Notes
how_to_run: brew install node rust # or from nodejs.org & rust-lang.org
notable: Skills method: predefined action recipes that use DOM tag attributes instead of runtime DOM manipulation by the LLM
Runs in the user's existing logged-in browser session without separate profiles
Hand-crafted recipes for Amazon, Gmail, Google, and Notion
Research mode that gathers, ranks, and cites sources
No vendor lock-in or API dependencies, per the README
caveats: Only Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge) are listed as supported; Firefox, Brave, Dia, and Comet are described as coming soon
Skills approach is stated as not infinitely scalable; the README says a scalability solution will be shared later
Requires a Gemini API key and a local Node.js and Rust toolchain to run
